rejected.headline: Martin County Fire Rescue faces $16.5M loss, 116 job cuts if property tax reform passes
rejected.source_title: Martin County leaders to hear how proposed property tax amendment could impact Fire Rescue - WPEC

lead_independence.headline: Martin County Fire Rescue faces $16.5M loss, 116 job cuts if property tax reform passes
lead_independence.lead: Martin County commissioners heard a presentation Tuesday outlining how a proposed expansion of Florida's homestead exemption could force Martin County Fire Rescue to cut 116 firefighters over the next two years if voters approve the constitutional amendment in November. The cuts would eliminate about one-third of the department's workforce due to reduced property tax revenue tied to the proposed amendment.

rejected.headline: Port St. Lucie could lose $48 million over two years if property tax amendment passes

lead_independence.headline: Port St. Lucie could lose $48 million over two years if property tax amendment passes
lead_independence.lead: During a summer budget workshop Thursday at the Port St. Lucie Community Center, City Manager Jesus Merejo told the City Council the city would lose the revenue if the item passes in November. To prepare for the potential hit, the city is deferring projects and holding the line on hiring. Port St. Lucie says it won't fund 184 requested positions, worth $28.3 million, including 25 new police officers and parks staff the city had already planned to add this year to keep up with growth at Torino Regional Park and the new BMX facility at Tradition Regional Park.

rejected.headline: New $70 million K-8 school breaks ground in Fort Pierce, will consolidate three St. Lucie County schools

lead_independence.headline: New $70 million K-8 school breaks ground in Fort Pierce, will consolidate three St. Lucie County schools
lead_independence.lead: A groundbreaking ceremony marked the start of construction on a new K-8 school in Fort Pierce that will combine three St. Lucie County schools into one state-of-the-art facility. The new school will be built on land behind Dan McCarty Middle School and is expected to welcome between 1,500 and 1,800 students when it opens. It will consolidate Dan McCarty Middle, St. Lucie Elementary and Lawnwood Elementary into a single campus.
